title: Arrange or Choose? Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Pick three of five friends for a photo in a row, or pick three of five friends for a picnic. Same friends, same number, but one answer is 60 and the other is 10. How do you know which formula to use? One simple question decides it every time: the swap test. This animated lesson follows NCERT Chapter 6, Permutations and Combinations (Class 11).

You will watch a live sorting machine run the swap test on six problems (a lock code, pizza toppings, a photo row, a handshake, a president and secretary, a committee) and drop each one into the Arrange bin or the Choose bin. Then we see why nPr = nCr x r!, watch groups and rows grow side by side, and use choose-then-arrange on mixed problems. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example that chooses boys and a girl and then seats them, the exam trap of forgetting to arrange, an original JEE Main pattern question on prizes, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
